packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-08 — unverified first image reading (blind; no identification seen in context)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview of face A)
- Three small separate parchment strips laid side by side on black ground, each roughly 7.5 cm wide x 5 cm high (by the scale bar). A glass weight rests on the left strip's upper right.
- Each strip carries a modern pencil shelfmark label along its lower edge (visible as "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-..." on the middle and right strips); the suffixes are not legible at this scale.
- All three show a small, dense gothic textualis book hand in brown/black ink, about 9-11 lines visible per strip, single block of text (no column edge visible at this scale; strips are probably cut-outs from a larger leaf, so no column structure can be inferred).
- The middle strip has many black worm holes / insect-damage holes.
- The right strip has a red rubric word in the middle of a line (about the 7th line), red ink.
- Left strip: text faded/abraded, darker staining.
- No running titles, enlarged initials, or marginal glosses visible at overview resolution. Orientation appears upright.
- Expect tiles image-002..004 to be native-resolution views of the three strips (left, middle, right).

========================================================================
image-002.jpg — native view of the LEFT strip (face A). Also shows the left edge of the middle strip at right of frame (not read here; read on its own tile).
Pencil label at foot: "Stams, StA, Frg. 256 3r" (suffix "3r" uncertain: could be 3r/3v).
Observations: about 9 text lines visible on the strip, written block runs from the left edge to about x=840; the right ~20% of the strip (x 840-1000) is blank margin -> this is the right-hand end of a text column with its outer margin. Lines at left edge are cut (start of line lost or illegible). Text very abraded and stained; ink faded to grey over most of the left half; the right half is better. Bottom ~third of strip below line 9 is blank/abraded (possibly lower margin or effaced text; one or two very faint traces under line 9 at left).
No rubric, no initial on this strip.
Crops: crop-01.jpg (whole text block, grey, autocontrast, 2x), crop-02.jpg (right half, blue channel, autocontrast, 3x). The blue channel crop was the most useful.

Lines numbered from top of the strip's text (line 1 at y~130 in image-002). Left portions mostly [illegible]; only the right-hand ends of lines are given with any confidence.
image-002 l.1: [illegible] nu?the? ... [illegible] ... [illegible]ttc?    (top edge damaged, torn notch at centre)
image-002 l.2: [illegible] ... [illegible] ... helle? fi?    (right end: "...elle? f"/"fi" cut by margin? uncertain)
image-002 l.3: [illegible] ... [illegible] ... regno? · uiui? p(er)?    ("regno" very uncertain; then a point; "uiui" or "uim"; then p with stroke)
image-002 l.4: [illegible] ... [illegible]a? ꝯ? archie? cuiuque?    (last word clearest: c-u-i/n-u-q-u-e, perhaps "cuiusque"/"cuiuque"; the word before ends "-che" or "-chie")
image-002 l.5: [illegible] ... [illegible] sp(er)? auro? · ꝯ? n̄? m?    (line end "-n̄ m" with a hyphen/line-filler)
image-002 l.6: o? [illegible] ... [illegible] ... at? · q(ui)? p(er)? uiue? / uīue?    (two abbreviated letters q and p with strokes, then "uiue" or "nine")
image-002 l.7: [illegible] ... [illegible] ... me · ex illo · s(cilicet)?    (clearest phrase on this strip: "ex illo"; final "s" with abbreviation / a "f" with stroke)
image-002 l.8: p? [illegible] ... ip?p(ri)a? ho(m)i(ni)s? · b(e)n(e)? · [hole] ...sine? / ...lt?ine
            (central words "ipp(ri)a"? then "hoīs" (h-o-i-s with suspension = hominis/homines?), then "bn" with points; a worm hole cuts the next word; line ends "-ine" or "-inte")
image-002 l.9: [illegible] ... cau?se? ... ꝯ? n̄? [hole] [.]mores? / amores? / timores?    (line end "-mores" fairly clear, preceding letter uncertain)
below l.9: faint traces only, [illegible].

Limitations: this strip's reading is very poor; nearly everything except the right halves of lines 3-9 is illegible at native resolution even with channel/contrast enhancement. Expansions are guesses at the abbreviation marks, not at the text.

========================================================================
image-003.jpg — native view of the MIDDLE strip (face A).
Pencil label: "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-2r".
Observations: two text blocks. (a) a main block from the cut left edge to about x=1000, about 10 lines (a partial line at the very top edge, then ~9 lines); (b) a narrow strip of a second text column at the far right (x ~1090-1220), separated by an intercolumn space at x ~1000-1090 -> the leaf was written in two columns; this strip preserves the right end of one column and the left beginnings of the next. A faint vertical ruling line appears near x~1000 (column boundary). Below the text (y>580) a blank area (lower margin, with the pencil label). Numerous worm holes. One small red trace at the left of the right column (about its 4th line, y~295 in image-003) - possibly a red stroke on an initial/paraph; not legible.
Ink extremely faded on this strip; only isolated words at the right side of the left block are legible.
Crops: crop-03.jpg (left block, blue channel, autocontrast, 2x), crop-04.jpg (right column strip, blue channel, 3x).

Left block (column a), lines from the top of the strip:
image-003 l.0: [cut top edge; tops of letters only] ...[illegible]...
image-003 l.1: [.]cessu?s? ... [hole] ... [illegible] ... ꝯ? / o meruerit? / inueniret?    (right end reads "-nieruere"/"meruere" with abbreviation; uncertain)
image-003 l.2: [illegible] ... [hole] ... en · ut? / at magis? / maior?    ("en ·" then "ut" or "at", then "maģ"/"magis")
image-003 l.3: [illegible] ... [hole] ... t?ho? / ūo de factā? / facta    ("de" fairly clear; next word f-a-c-t/f-e-c-t with suspension)
image-003 l.4: [illegible] p(ro)? ... [illegible] ... cu? ... in illis? ꝯ?
image-003 l.5: f? ... [illegible]
image-003 l.6: [illegible]
image-003 l.7: [illegible] ... [illegible] ... laudi? / fand? ... [hole]
image-003 l.8: [illegible]p(er)? ... [hole] ... ꝗ? ... s? nono? / menor?    ("-nono"/"-nore" clear letters, preceded by a long s or f)
image-003 l.9: numero? / mundo? ꝯ? fe? fac? [illegible] ... [illegible] ... ord? de? aliq(ui)? / alium?

Right column (column b), beginnings of lines only (letter clusters):
image-003 rc l.1: [illegible]
image-003 rc l.2: m? / uir?
image-003 rc l.3: fed? / sed? (red trace near here in colour image)
image-003 rc l.4: c? ... [illegible]
image-003 rc l.5: [illegible]d? / ad?
image-003 rc l.6: an?
image-003 rc l.7: uih? / nih?
image-003 rc l.8: ugn? / magn?
image-003 rc l.9: [illegible]

Limitations: almost entirely illegible; the above is letter-level at best and should not be relied on for matching except perhaps "de fact-" (l.3) and "-nono" (l.8).

========================================================================
image-004.jpg — native view of the RIGHT strip (face A). Also shows the right edge of the middle strip at far left of frame (ignored).
Pencil label: "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-1r".
Observations: wide blank left margin (x ~280-500), then a text block running to the cut right edge (text continues past the right edge; line ends lost). About 10 lines plus a partial line of tops at the top edge. Lines 4-5 and 8 begin indented relative to lines 1-3, 6-7, 9-10 (could be indentation for an initial or a quoted/verse passage; or simply abrasion of the line starts - the indentation on lines 4-5 looks real, staggered). Line 8 has a red rubric in mid-line (about x 880-1110): red letters followed by a red C-shaped mark/paragraph sign with a tail. Below line 10, blank lower margin with the pencil label. Ink brown, moderately faded; better than the other two strips.
Crops: crop-05.jpg (left half of text, colour, autocontrast, 3x), crop-06.jpg (right half, colour, autocontrast, 3x). Upscaling did not add much; native image-004 was about as useful.

Lines from top of strip (l.0 = cut tops at the top edge):
image-004 l.0:  [tops of letters only] ...p?... [illegible]
image-004 l.1:  tamn? / [.]amen? · ꝯ? · d? ... [illegible] ... [illegible] ... e?cin? / ecui?
image-004 l.2:  fecit? / fectu? b(e)n(e)? re? ... [illegible] ... tetu? / fecit?   ("fecit bn̄" / "fectū bn̄" at line start fairly visible; "bn̄" = bene?)
image-004 l.3:  lep(ro)? / leg(?) ... [illegible] ... re · ꝯ? b? iterū? / item eo · facio? / factō?   ("eo ·" then f-a-c-i-o/f-a-c-t-o with mark)
image-004 l.4:     (indented) ecc?ia? / eiusmodi? ... [illegible]m? illius? acq(ui)si? / accepit?
image-004 l.5:      (indented further) tum? n? sic? · ut a?mice? / amice? rea?[...]   ("· ut" clear)
image-004 l.6:  infra? / ipsa? an?[...] ... [illegible] negocio? / negotio? ... [illegible] ...
image-004 l.7:  ue(n)tu? / negotiu? manu? / ma(n)u · male? / mole? sc? / fe? b? [...]
image-004 l.8:     (indented) nae? / hac? i(n) libl?o / libro? ·   RED: [.]l[.]llaus? / llans? followed by a red C-shaped sign (capitulum/paragraph mark) with a red tail stroke   ... [illegible] ... a?
image-004 l.9:  stb? / sic? le? mane(n)t? / mane(re)? ... ꝯ? / q(uod)? ... [illegible] ... e? ... [illegible]
image-004 l.10: c? ... [illegible]...b? anon? / an(n)o(rum)? d? / de? ... [illegible]...ince(?)ra? / [illegible]

Limitations: readings are letter-level and many word divisions uncertain. The red rubric is best seen in image-004 at native scale and crop-06.jpg; I cannot read it confidently (the letters look like "l l l a u s" with a ligature, perhaps ending "-laus" or "-lans").

End of face A (images 001-004). Images 005-008 follow (face B).

========================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (image-005.jpg, overview of face B = versos)
- The same three strips turned over: left labelled "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-3v" (label readable), middle and right labels faint (presumably 2v, 1v). Two glass weights on the left strip.
- Versos are darker brown, stained, with rust-coloured spotting. Text block ~8-10 lines each, same small gothic book hand; the text on the left and right strips looks darker/clearer than on the rectos. Middle strip again worm-holed.
- No rubric or initial visible at overview scale. Tiles image-006..008 are expected to be the three versos.

========================================================================
image-006.jpg — native view of the LEFT verso, label "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-3v" (white ink).
Observations: blank left margin (x ~150-340), text block x ~340 to the cut right edge at ~1145 (line ends lost on the right). 9 lines of text (y ~195-610), then blank lower area with label. Heavy brown staining. One small red stroke mid-line on l.6 (x~810) - a red touch on a letter (rubricated capital / paraph stroke). Top edge torn at x~570. Worm slits.
Since 3r (image-002) had a right margin and 3v has a left margin, recto and verso are consistent with the same column seen from both sides.
Crops: crop-07.jpg (left half, red channel, autocontrast, 3x), crop-08.jpg (right half, same). The red channel suppressed the brown stain well; this was the most readable surface in the packet so far.

image-006 l.1: m?aiorem? / [.]iorem · [tear] p(ro)pt(er)? ... ꝯ? aliquoꝝ? z / (et) p(ro)prio? / p(ro)pa? ... al[...]   ("aliquo-" fairly clear; then a z-shaped et/-rum? then ꝓp...)
image-006 l.2: [.]n? ... [hole] ... p(er)fecti? / peccati? · tunc? / mac? ꝯbint(ur)? / cōbinit? · ui? ... [illegible] ... fi?
image-006 l.3: re? / ce? autē nos obtine(re)? / obtinē(?) glo(ria)? / glīa? p(er)? · ad? ... [illegible] ... m?
image-006 l.4: uel? / nl · ūq̄? / u(e)l q(uod)? d(omi)n(u)s / dn̄s qu(i)? ad du[...] / [.]n̄d̄ne? q(uod)? fe? illi? / sibi? ... [illegible]
image-006 l.5: [.]nicela? / [.]ticula? ꝯ n̄ / n(on) erat? de? / eradeuis? / erat deinde?[.] · d(e)? continēt? / dic(itu)r? ꝯ? ... ua?
image-006 l.6: ce(r)tius? / eternis? / ceteris? gesti? / gestis? ... [red stroke] ... n(on)? / nō · ꝯ? · in h(oc)? a?
image-006 l.7: i(n)ternos? / ipsius? ꝯ? / (et)? ... ait? / ug(?)? f? · gr(ati)a? / q(uo)? ... ꝯtuo? / sitio? ... · iure? / aure?
image-006 l.8: g? / si · d(ic)tum? / eclm? · u? · p(ro)pria? / ꝓpria · sibi? ... u(e)l? / n̄ · ce(r)? ... sc? / fe? ... [illegible]
image-006 l.9: q? ... a? ... ca? [hole] ... tantam? / tanitia? mē? / me? ꝯ ... gra? ... [illegible] ... rel(?)?[...]

Limitations: word division and many letters uncertain; the stain obscures the centre (around x 600-900, l.4-l.8).

========================================================================
image-007.jpg — native view of the MIDDLE verso, label "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-2v" (white/grey ink; last character uncertain).
Observations: two text columns. (a) column a: only the line ENDS survive, along the left cut edge (x ~235-380); (b) intercolumn space x ~380-490; (c) column b from x ~490 to the cut right edge (~1250), line ends lost. About 9 lines (y ~165-580), blank lower margin below with label. Many worm holes. Mirrors 2r (image-003), where column a's line ends and column b's line starts were seen from the other side; here column a line ends sit on the left, consistent with a leaf flip.
Crops: crop-09.jpg (column a line-ends, red channel, 3x), crop-10.jpg (column b left half), crop-11.jpg (column b right half); all red channel, autocontrast, 3x.

Column a (line ends only):
image-007 a l.1: [.]ceg? / [.]ceo?
image-007 a l.2: [.]iniur? / [.]nibar? / inuar?
image-007 a l.3: [.]yse? / [.]ge?
image-007 a l.4: [.]o · an-   (hyphen at line end)
image-007 a l.5: [.]uano? / uāno / uand?
image-007 a l.6: [.]alior / aliō?
image-007 a l.7: [.]o · eu? / cu?
image-007 a l.8: [.]nans? / -mand? / -nand
image-007 a l.9: [.]umm? / -nunt?

Column b:
image-007 b l.1: [illegible] ... u? ... e(n)t? / est? · liba? / libe(r)? ... [hole] ... p? ... [hole] ... ead?
image-007 b l.2: quid? / quiꝫ? · n(on)? / ē? ... ite? / itez? · ē? ... [hole] ... grauē? / exemp(l)ū? ... · ei? / tu? · si? / oſ?
image-007 b l.3: solūe? / solue(re)? ... u? z? a? ... [hole] ... ens? · ... omīa? / aliu? et?
image-007 b l.4: h? · i? ... ratio? / arid? · ca(us)a? / ꝗ? p(er)? ... [illegible] ... ꝗ? ... q? · ...
image-007 b l.5: eꝫ? / ꝯtg? ani(m)a? / an̄a? ... uo? / tuo? / mo? · uol? ... [illegible] ... ip(s)us? / ip(s)is? ꝗ? d?
image-007 b l.6: i[hole] ... ius? / mo? · reputa(n)t? / reputa(m)? / uestam? ... [hole] ... unus? / uim? ... amo? / anno?
image-007 b l.7: [illegible] ... · ꝗ? · dat? / dicit? / dt? · ani? / cui? ... [hole] ... in? / ui? ... (con)? ... o? ...
image-007 b l.8: u? ... ra? ... ꝯ? magna? / mag(is)? ... [hole] ... ambꝫ? / omnibus? ... rre? / uū? ... ali? / uik?
image-007 b l.9: a? ... tum? / cuꝫ? · u? ... p(ro)? redde? / reddi? ... ꝯtinens? / co(n)tinet? s? · p? ...

Limitations: very uncertain throughout; holes take out letters in l.2-l.8. Only "an-" (a l.4), "-alior" (a l.6), "quid" (b l.2), "solue" (b l.3), "reputa-" (b l.6) and "redde-" (b l.9) are moderately secure.

========================================================================
image-008.jpg — native view of the RIGHT verso, label "Stams, StA, Frg. 256-1v".
Observations: text block from the cut LEFT edge (x~160; line beginnings lost) to x~990, then a blank right margin (x ~990-1170). 10 lines (y ~185-625), blank lower margin below with label. Consistent with 1r (image-004), which had a left margin: same column seen from the other side. A tiny red dot on l.7 (x~705) - red touch on a letter. Stained but the clearest surface in the packet. Text shows many short abbreviated tokens separated by points, of the pattern "l · ... ff ... neg̃ · g̃ ..." (looks like reference/allegation style: letter "l" with points, "ff"-like sign, numerals) - observation only; I have not tried to identify.
Crops: crop-12.jpg (left half, red channel, autocontrast, 3x), crop-13.jpg (right half, same).

image-008 l.1:  [.]etiam? / eciam? / tam? ꝗ? · l · u? · ꝓpria? / p(ri)ma? / p(ro)pri[...] ... [illegible] ... ꝗ? · ego? / ergo? · ...
image-008 l.2:  s? / ſ a magist(ra)tu? / a ma[.]i[.]tratu? e(st)? · ut? / uel? ... [illegible] ... ꝯ? ff? · d(e)? / g? · ꝯtra? / contra?

image-008 l.5:  [.]e?c?lie? / quale? · eius? / ai(us)? · n(on) / ū · sp(on)te? / ſpōte · admi(ni)strat(i)o(n)e? / administrator?
image-008 l.6:  [.]uerit? / fecerit? int(er)? ... s(us)pitione? / suſpi(ci)one? / suspicione · h(ab)ebis? / he(re)dis? · leg? / lex? neg(otiorum)? / neg̃?
image-008 l.7:  [.]na(n)t? / dat? q(ui)? ue? · ee? / ē? · ꝯ? · neg̃ · g̃ · l · ai? / an? / ar? ꝓ? / f? · in? / tu?   (red dot near "neg̃")
image-008 l.8:  l · adq(ui)r? / a dq? ... [illegible] ... s? / ff? · 9? / D? · ꝗ? ... l · ex? / reo? ... eccl(es)ia? / flag? / leg̃? · q(u)a? / q(ua)m? ...
image-008 l.9:  ꝗ? / quis? / sui? mutuans? / mutuatus? / mand(at)us? · n̄ / ui? · ad? / ai? ꝯ? / e? · natiuꝫ? / nauticus? / mutuus? · uel? / ūd?
image-008 l.10: [.]uit? / qui? · sacramentum? / s[.]uuntdem? ... [illegible] ... amissio? / auicus? ... [illegible]

Limitations: the words "a magistratu" (l.2), "sponte administr-" (l.4, l.5; "spōte" visible twice), "suspicione/suspitione" (l.6), "neg̃ · g̃" (l.3/l.7), "mutua-" (l.9) are the more secure readings; everything else is tentative. Line beginnings on this strip are lost at the cut left edge.

========================================================================
SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS
- 3 strips, both faces, one hand (small gothic textualis), at least partly two-column (middle strip shows an intercolumn space on both faces). Strip 1 (labels 1r/1v): column with left margin on r, right margin on v. Strip 3 (3r/3v): right margin on r, left margin on v. Strip 2: two columns on both faces. Red: rubric word + paragraph/capitulum sign on 1r l.8; small red touches on 2r, 3v l.6, 1v l.7.
- Recto surfaces (002-004) are badly faded; 002 and 003 are almost unreadable. Verso surfaces (006-008) are stained but readable in the red channel; 008 (1v) gives the best text.
- Unread: line beginnings/ends lost at the cut edges of every strip; most of the left halves on 002 and 003. A multispectral/UV image would be needed for 2r and 3r.
- Every reading here is unverified and many letters are guesses; expansions in parentheses are suggestions from abbreviation marks only.
- No identification was revealed in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules other than making crops (crop-01 .. crop-13.jpg) in the private scratch folder. All images were viewed without hitting the image limit.
